To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the ontology-based approach is effective in assisting BPR by identifying the causes of inefficiencies; (ii) the ontology-based BPR approach has been applied in a university domain to identify the cause of inefficiency of the business processes in the university domain; and (iii) the ontology-based methodology can be used to assist BPR in other domains.
the use of a knowledge map can assist in the identification and understanding of the inefficiencies in a business process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ontology based knowledge maps as a means of assisting in the identification of the causes of the problems in BPR and the improvement of business processes.

the development of a methodology and a tool for BPR that will overcome the two obstacles of the lack of consideration of the organizational context and lack of tools for automatically identifying the cause of inefficient processes.

the following issues: (i) How to represent the knowledge of the organization formally to support an inferencing mechanism for identifying the causes of the business process inefficiencies; (ii) How to use a formal representation of the knowledge of the organizational domain to support the BPR methodology and to provide the knowledge maps to assist in the BPR process; (iii) How to develop a methodology for using the ontology and knowledge maps in the BPR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the methodology proposed in this paper has the following benefits: • The use of the ontology and the knowledge maps allows for the identification of the knowledge sources, which are relevant to the business process and the environment in which the business process operates.
the ontology based knowledge maps provide a means of identifying the causes of inconsistencies and inefficiencies and the means of improving the performance of the business process.
the proposed methodology for BPR is a promising approach for assisting organizations to re-engineer their business processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ontology based knowledge map is an important step towards the development of a tool that would assist in business process re-engineing.
we have developed and evaluated the methodology and tools to help organizations to improve the efficiency, quality, and consistency of their business process re-engineerings.
we have developed and evaluated a knowledge management methodology that can help to improve BPR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ontology-based knowledge maps can be used to support business process re-engineerings by helping identify the causes of inefficiencies and inconsistencies and by providing a knowledge structure for the organization that is useful for the BPR.

ontology-based knowledge maps can be used to improve the effectiveness of BPR by making knowledge visible to stakeholders, and to support the automated identification of inefficiencies in business processes.

the ontology and the knowledge structure can be used to support business process reengineering (BPR) by providing a means for representing and reasoning with the organizational knowledge that can be used to identify the causes of inefficiencies and inconsistencies within an organization.
